newsitem.title: USA: Cooper Hospital, N.J., confirms federal probe.
newsitem.headline: Cooper Hospital, N.J., confirms federal probe.

text.p: Officials at Cooper Hospital-University Medical Center in Camden, N.J., confirmed Thursday that a federal prosecutor is investigating a $69 million bond deal sold in February.

"The Cooper Health System is cooperating fully in the investigation undertaken by the U.S. Attorney and stands prepared to provide whatever further assistance might be requested," Sharon Clark, a hospital spokeswoman, said in an interview.
The Philadelphia Inquirer reported the probe Thursday, saying it centers on whether the hospital adequately disclosed to potential bond buyers significant losses from fraud.
The bonds were underwritten by Lehman Brothers, a unit of Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc, and sold through the Camden County Improvement Authority.
Lehman Brothers could not be reached for comment.
The Improvement Authority said in a statement that the Federal Bureau of Investigation had requested a copy of the bond deal prospectus.

"We cooperated fully with the request for information and were assured that the Camden County Improvement Authority -- including directors and staff -- is not the subject of any investigation," Philip Rowan, the authority's executive director, said.
The Securities and Exchange Commission has not contacted either the hospital or the authority for information on the bond deal, officials at Cooper Hospital and the authority said.
FBI officials refused to confirm or deny the existence of the investigation.

In the secondary market Thursday, a block of the bonds in question, Cooper Hospital 5.875 percent bonds of 2015, was offered at 6.15 percent. Kenny Evaluation Services Inc priced the bonds at Wednesday's close at 6.22 percent.
